description:
Seldon Expedition: Beyond the Predicted.

Unimos ciência, tecnologia e criatividade para transformar dados reais em soluções. Inspirados em Hari Seldon (Fundação, Asimov): prever padrões é valioso; ir além deles gera descoberta.
Clima colaborativo, foco em aprender e entregar.

Buscamos: desenvolvimento de software, design (UI/UX, ilustração), ciência e dados, roteiro/storytelling e apresentação/vídeo.

Não precisa ser especialista: curiosidade já conta muito.
summary:
Ankerona: Mars Mission is a free, pixel-art browser game that turns NASA’s open Mars data into a walk across Gale Crater. You play Ana Selari, a geologist on a hypothetical mission, guided by Tatu, a cargo rover that leads the way and gathers the mission data in one panel. Along the route you manage oxygen and radiation, cross soft sand, avoid sharp rocks and survive a solar particle event. Each discovery unlocks a Field Guide entry with the real data and its source.

This answers the “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map” challenge by joining data from several NASA missions in a single view that helps someone on the surface plan and carry out a walk safely. It matters because NASA holds huge amounts of open data that most people never see: one archive alone holds about 390 TB. Ankerona makes that data playable, so learning happens through play, with no download or installation.
details:
What it does. The player leaves the habitat, follows Tatu to a series of targets in Gale Crater and records discoveries in the Field Guide. Hazards come from real mission experience: sharp rocks (the damaged wheels of Curiosity), soft sand (Spirit getting stuck in 2009), dust (the 2018 storm that ended Opportunity) and radiation. Tatu’s panel brings together the current target briefing, the Field Guide, weather, radiation, the sound of the Martian wind and a schematic crater map. In an emergency, Tatu aborts the walk and takes Ana back to the habitat.

Benefits and intended impact. Anyone with a browser can explore real Mars science for free. Every scientific fact carries a source line, and the game itself says which values are simulated (the crew, dose rates, the weather panel and the illustrative terrain). We want to lower the barrier between open NASA data and the public, especially students.

Tools. Phaser 4, TypeScript and Vite, with pixel-art sprites and the Press Start 2P and VT323 fonts. The game is hosted on Vercel. Terrain is derived from HiRISE digital terrain models. The documentation and bilingual README (English and Portuguese-BR) are on GitHub under the MIT license.

Creative aspect. The name Ankerona joins the first syllables of the CHAPEA 1 crew (Anca, Kelly, Ross, Nathan), NASA’s first one-year Mars simulation. The characters are a tribute to that crew. The guide is a rover named Tatu, the Brazilian word for armadillo.

Factors considered. Scientific accuracy over spectacle, clear separation between real and simulated data, accessibility (runs in the browser, no cost) and a scope that a six-person team could finish in two days.
